country.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
country.peg: The dobra has been pegged to the euro at 24.5 STN per EUR since 2010; confirm current central-bank rate before any conversion.

purpose: Country evidence inventory for later crop-specific enterprise budgets. Not a calculator input file and not authority to activate the country.

evidence_sections.source_name: FAO São Tomé and Príncipe country overview

observations.finding: FAO country overview states agriculture employs more than 65% of the population.
FAO overview describes cocoa as dominant and contributing about 90% of exports.
Cassava, maize and banana are highlighted as priority food production crops.
FAO overview reports an older estimate that livestock contributes 14% of agricultural production and 3% of GDP; the underlying household estimate dates to 2002.

caveats: The 65% employment and 90% export shares are broad sector context, not farm-level productivity or income measures.
The livestock contribution estimate is dated and should not be used as a current indicator.

evidence_sections.topic: national statistical system and data access
evidence_sections.source_name: Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) São Tomé e Príncipe

observations.finding: INE provides thematic statistics including external trade, consumer price index, economy and national data/SDG portals.
INE portal reports provisional population from the 2024 population and housing census.

caveats: The accessible portal page confirms statistical topics and headline indicators, but crop-by-crop production, area and farmgate price tables were not extracted in this review.
CPI inflation is not a crop price or agricultural input cost series.

evidence_sections.source_name: FAOSTAT data as displayed by secondary country-series pages
caveats: These are secondary displays of FAOSTAT observations, not direct extracts from the official FAOSTAT bulk dataset; verify original series, item codes, flags and units before calculator use.
The displayed cassava values are rounded; do not treat approximate rounded figures as exact national statistics.
Coffee output is extremely small in the secondary series and flagged as estimated.

evidence_sections.source_name: Commo Atlas country commodity page, citing USDA PSD, FAOSTAT and trade data
evidence_sections.reference_date: data page crawled 2026-10-30; cocoa marketing year 2024/25
caveats: The 4,000 tonne cocoa production figure differs materially from a government country portal claim of 15,000 tonnes/year and from FAO's description of cocoa's export dominance. These numbers may differ by scope, year, cocoa beans versus processed products, or source methodology; reconcile against FAOSTAT, USDA PSD and national customs/producer data.
Export values are not farmgate prices and cannot be used as XAF/STN/kg or STN/kg producer prices.

evidence_sections.topic: official government sector overview and exchange-rate reference
evidence_sections.source_name: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe country information portal
evidence_sections.reference_date: portal accessed 2026-11-01; exchange-rate reference dated March 2025

observations.finding: Official currency is the dobra (STN). Government page reports a fixed rate of 24.5 STN per EUR, with reference rates updated March 2025.
Government portal highlights cocoa and coffee, and mentions vanilla as artisanal production.

caveats: The government's 15,000 tonnes/year cocoa claim conflicts with the 4,000 tonnes 2024/25 secondary production series. Do not use either as a calculator parameter until scope and source data are reconciled.
The displayed exchange-rate date is March 2025; obtain a current central-bank rate for any live conversion.

evidence_sections.topic: producer decision-making and farm cost constraints
evidence_sections.source_name: University of Évora repository, 2026 master's thesis on cocoa price fluctuations and producer investment decisions

observations.finding: Mixed-method study using historical cocoa production and price data for 1999–2023 and semi-structured interviews with six local cocoa producers.
The study abstract reports that producers increase spending on labour and crop-protection products during high-price periods and reduce expenditure/rely on family labour during low-price periods.
The abstract identifies limited access to agricultural credit, lack of continuous technical assistance and weak institutional monitoring as constraints.

caveats: The interview sample is six producers and is not a nationally representative enterprise budget.
The thesis abstract does not provide a complete current unit-cost schedule or validated farmgate price series.

evidence_sections.topic: food import dependence and price transmission
evidence_sections.source_name: World Food Programme country page and IMF Selected Issues 2025
evidence_sections.reference_date: WFP page accessed 2026-11-01; IMF report published 8 August 2025

observations.finding: WFP identifies geographic isolation, a small domestic market and dependence on imports as structural vulnerabilities.
IMF reports nearly half of food items in the CPI basket are locally produced; imported food price movements also affect domestic inflation.

caveats: Import dependence and CPI composition help explain market conditions but do not provide crop-specific producer prices.
The 2023 inflation rate is historical and should not be substituted for 2026 inflation.

evidence_sections.source_name: European Commission, Agri-food trade with São Tomé and Príncipe

observations.item: EU agri-food imports from São Tomé and Príncipe
Change in EU agri-food imports from STP

caveats: These are bilateral EU trade values, not total national agricultural exports, producer prices or farm revenues.

evidence_sections.topic: newly presented 2025/26 agricultural census results and national structural indicators
evidence_sections.source_name: Rádio Somos Todos Primos (RSTP), reporting the Ministry of Agriculture presentation of the Third General Agricultural Census; cross-check: Téla Nón

observations.caveat: Not stated to be current harvested area, cultivated area, or crop-specific area; do not calculate yields from this figure.

observations.item: Rural population with agriculture as principal occupation
observations.caveat: Denominator and operational definition are not fully specified in the article; do not equate with share of national population or agricultural workforce.
Broad food availability statement; not a crop yield or self-sufficiency ratio for each commodity.

observations.finding: The coordinator stated that the census report contains production by crop, area by crop, livestock numbers, rural conditions and production-support infrastructure. The public articles reviewed report headline indicators but do not reproduce the crop-by-crop tables.

caveats: The census results were presented by the Ministry of Agriculture on 4 September 2026; the numerical values in this evidence record are transcribed from press coverage of that presentation, not from the complete primary census tables.
The 38,020 hectares are described as land designated for agriculture, not as harvested area; they cannot be used as the denominator for crop yields.
Livestock stock counts are not annual offtake, meat production, egg output, or enterprise productivity.

The census coordinator identified poor rural road access as a constraint on moving produce to markets; this supports including transport and market-access costs in future budgets but does not quantify them.
Obtain the full census report and metadata, then extract crop x district x area x production tables and verify definitions, reference period, weights and survey design.

evidence_sections.topic: cocoa export unit value as trade-price cross-check only
evidence_sections.source_name: UN Comtrade export unit value as presented by Selina Wamucii
caveats: The 64.37 STN/kg figure is an export unit value, not a farmgate producer price; it includes export-chain composition and must not be used as a farm revenue assumption.

The displayed 2024 production and harvested-area/yield figures on the secondary page are internally inconsistent: 4,000 tonnes divided by 43,874 hectares is about 0.091 tonnes/ha, not the displayed 0.01 tonnes/ha. Verify the original FAOSTAT item, area and yield series before use.
The 4,000-tonne 2024 estimate conflicts with the government portal's earlier 15,000-tonne/year cocoa claim; preserve both as conflicting claims until primary data resolves scope and period.

calculator_data_gaps: Obtain official INE/MADR crop production and harvested-area tables by island, district, crop and production year, preferably from agricultural census or crop surveys.
Verify FAOSTAT 2024 crop output and yield values directly against original dataset downloads and retain observation flags.
Resolve the cocoa production discrepancy between the government portal's 15,000 tonnes/year and the secondary 2024/25 estimate of 4,000 tonnes.
Collect dated farmgate cocoa prices in STN/kg by quality, fermentation/drying status, cooperative and island; distinguish export FOB prices and world cocoa benchmarks.
Collect current producer prices for cassava, banana, maize, plantain, vegetables, coffee and other candidate crops by location, unit and season.
Obtain input quotations for planting material, fertiliser, crop protection, labour, land preparation, transport, drying/fermentation, packaging and irrigation.
Construct crop-specific enterprise budgets and yields for smallholder systems; separately model cocoa perennial establishment and mature-year production.
Confirm current exchange rate and any island-specific logistics costs before converting imported inputs or export values.
Obtain the full Third General Agricultural Census report presented on 4 September 2026; transcribe crop-by-district cultivated/harvested area, production and yields with metadata and definitions.

Verify reported census headline totals (38,020 ha, 20,084 agricultural workers, 1,033 cattle, approximately 556,000 poultry and 42,000 pigs) against the primary report; do not treat land designated for agriculture as harvested area.
Reconcile cocoa output and area/yield inconsistencies against original FAOSTAT and national census tables; export unit values remain non-farmgate.

activation_blockers: No validated current farmgate crop price series
No complete crop-specific input quotations or enterprise budgets
National crop area and production tables not yet extracted
Cocoa production figures conflict and require source reconciliation
Third General Agricultural Census headline results are now reported publicly, but full crop-by-district tables and primary report metadata have not yet been extracted.

safeguards: Research-only evidence; not a live calculator dataset.
Do not activate São Tomé and Príncipe or change calculator formulas based on this file.
Do not substitute world cocoa benchmark prices, export unit values, consumer prices or national CPI for producer farmgate prices.
Do not treat the secondary FAOSTAT presentation as the primary data source.

evidence.topic: INE 2017 statistical yearbook: agricultural production and livestock series
evidence.source: Instituto Nacional de Estatística, São Tomé e Príncipe em Números 2017
caveats: These are historical national series published in a 2017 yearbook, not current 2026 observations.
The agricultural summary does not supply crop area, so no yield can be calculated.
The table heading and source attribute the series to MADR/INE; confirm units and definitions against underlying ministry records before calculator mapping.
The cocoa entry is labelled chocolate in the source table and must not be silently relabelled as raw cocoa beans.

evidence.topic: Administrative geography, current census activity and currency context

observations.status: Government of São Tomé and Príncipe
Government page reports Central Bank rate updated March 2025

caveats: INE describes seven districts and separately states that Príncipe has autonomous-region status; Pagué remains the district entry in the seven-district list.
The second phase of the 2025 agricultural census was reported as underway in May 2026; no final crop tables were found in this review.
The dobra peg is reported by the government page with a March 2025 update date; obtain current Banco Central confirmation before using a live conversion rate.

missing_data_before_calculator_use: Obtain the final 2025 General Agricultural Census tables, including crop area, production, yield, season and district.
Obtain current district-level farmgate prices, planting-material costs, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, machinery, irrigation and energy costs.
Build current crop-specific enterprise budgets and calculator tests.
Verify historical agricultural table definitions and units against MADR source records before use.
